thread.title: It's The Best Time In 3 Years To Buy Dividend King 3M - 3M Company (NYSE:MMM)

author: Dividend Sensei
title: It's The Best Time In 3 Years To Buy Dividend King 3M - 3M Company (NYSE:MMM)
text:
(Source: imgflip )
I analyze over 200 companies each year in my never-ending hunt for great long-term dividend growth ideas. Readers are frequently asking me "what are the best stocks to buy right now". So to help income investors know the best place for new money at any given time, I've recently launched my new series, tracking the Deep Value Dividend Growth Portfolio or DVDGP. This paper portfolio is designed with my average reader in mind and is 100% composed of what I consider sleep well at night or SWAN stocks.
That means companies with safe dividends, good long-term growth prospects, and that are trading at great prices. The companies themselves are chosen from four different watchlists, high-yield blue-chips, fast dividend growers, dividend aristocrats/kings, and my bear market buy list (quality dividend stocks that will generate 13+% total returns if bought at low enough valuations). The first three watchlists are focused on the most undervalued stocks in each category each week.
Dividend Aristocrats Vs S&P 500
(Source: Ploutos Research)
The reason I chose to make the aristocrats one of the focused watchlists is because of their great track record of delivering superior long-term returns, all with far less volatility than the S&P 500.
Thanks to the market's most recent severe correction (which now threatens to become a non-recessionary bear market), dividend king (60 consecutive years of dividend hikes) 3M ( MMM ) is now on sale.
MMM data by YCharts In fact, while the broader market merely flirts with bear market territory, 3M is firmly entrenched in one.
MMM Dividend Yield (TTM) data by YCharts As a result, this legendary industrial blue-chip now trades at its most attractive valuation in three years.
So let's take a closer look at why Wall Street has become so bearish on this dividend king, but more importantly why those worries are likely overblown. In fact, there are three reasons why I just added 3M to the DVDGP and you should also consider buying this proven SWAN stock for your portfolio. That's because from today's attractive price (about 17% undervalued) 3M is likely to not just deliver safe and steadily growing dividends over the years, but also market-beating long-term 14.5% total returns as well.
Why Wall Street Is Bearish On 3M Based on its horrible recent performance, you might think that 3M's latest results were catastrophic. In fact, they were not.
Metric Q3 2018 Results Revenue Growth -0.2% Net Income Growth 8.0% Free Cash Flow Growth 23.6% Shares Outstanding -4.4% EPS Growth 10.7% FCF/Share Growth 29.4% Dividend Growth 15.7% (Sources: Earnings Release, Morningstar)
While flat revenue growth is never a good thing, the company managed to deliver strong EPS growth. More importantly, free cash flow, what's left over after running the business and investing in future growth, boomed. FCF is what pays for buybacks and dividends, and is the most important metric for income investors to focus on. As a result of solid growth in its bottom line, 3M has delivered great dividend growth this year, rewarding long-term dividend lovers with what they care about most.
So why is Wall Street hammering on 3M right now? Well, one reason was that Q3's results missed analyst expectations .
revenue fell short by 3% adjusted EPS missed by 8% In addition, management lowered full-year adjusted EPS guidance by 4%. This new guidance would mean that for 2018 3M will likely miss analyst consensus EPS estimates by 3%.
Three things are weighing on 3M's results in the near-term .
Low-single-digit or negative organic local-currency growth across all business segments. Weakness in all markets except Asia-Pacific (which reported 3% organic volume growth). Foreign exchange headwinds. Many of these factors are attributed to slowing global growth which is being made worse by America's ongoing trade war with China (a major cause of the current severe market correction). Global manufacturing has indeed slowed to its lowest growth rate in three years, which the market worries will weigh heavily on 3M's sales and earnings growth in 2019.
(Source: Bloomberg)
Another headwind is that the Enterprise Resource Planning or ERP, which boosted first-half revenue growth by 1% , will now no longer be providing that tailwind.
Add to that rising US interest rates are helping to push up the dollar relative to other major global currencies and currency translation knocked 1.7% off 3M's top line and resulted in some very disappointing organic currency adjusted segment performance.
(Sources: earnings release, Motley Fool)
In total, 3M posted just 1% organic growth, which is a far cry from last year's Q3 growth of 7%. Healthcare especially delivered results that management called "softer than expected". Healthcare and its consumer segment have struggled in recent years to live up to the company's earlier long-term forecasts. Combined with weaker than expected results in its electronics and energy segments (mostly due to a slowing economy), management lowered its guidance yet again for the full year, which it has been doing every quarter in 2018.
(Source: Motley Fool)
And mind you the company's exposure to cyclical industries, especially energy, means that in the event of an oil crash (or other industrial recession) its organic growth guidance can come in below expectations. That's what happened in 2015 and 2016 when oil prices crashed 76% and helped drag down the company's results far below initial guidance.
(Source: Motley Fool)
With oil prices recently crashing 40% from recent highs, the market may be fearful that 2019 (and possibly beyond) may see another industrial recession. And given that 2019 guidance is hardly sensational, this explains a great deal of the market's recent pessimism for the stock.
For 2019 guidance calls for 1%-3% total sales growth and 2%-4% organic local currency sales growth. However, thanks to ongoing cost-cutting efforts 3M still expects that to translate to adjusted EPS growth of 7% to 11% and 100% of that is expected to be converted to free cash flow. As I'll explain later, those results are just slightly below management's newest long-term forecast.
Basically, 3M's shares are being walloped because it's a cyclical company and is likely facing macro induced headwinds that mean that the next year or two will see slower growth than it's enjoyed in 2017 and 2018. But here is what Wall Street is missing and why now is actually a great time for long-term dividend growth investors to cash in on the market's short-term focus and rising pessimism about 3M.
1. The Fundamentals Remain Strong And Long-Term Growth Plans On Track It's important to remember that all industrial company sales and earnings are cyclical over time.
(Source: Simply Safe Dividends)
Minnesota Mining & Manufacturing or 3M was founded in 1902 and over the past 117 years has managed to become one of the world's most dominant industrial conglomerates by adapting to changing global economic and industry conditions. That includes growth via both organic R&D induced product launches, as well as bolt-on acquisitions. The result is the company sells over 60,000 products in over 70 countries around the world.
3M is masterfully run, and willing to discontinue product lines that are no longer earning sufficient returns on invested capital. The company has streamlined its operations in recent years from 40 to 23 divisions and sold off 10 underperforming businesses for $2.1 billion. 3M has about 200 manufacturing plants around the world, each being about four to five times larger than the industry average. Those plants are about 43% more efficient than smaller ones, and the company's distribution centers (also very large and automated) are about 23% more efficient than those of its rivals'.
This allows it to generate much lower cost inputs than many of its peers. These economies of scale, combined with premium pricing on its patented products, is what allows 3M to be one of the most profitable industrial companies on earth.
Company Operating Margin Net Margin FCF Margin Return On Invested Capital
3M 21% 19% 13% 27% Industry Average 7% 5% NA 6% (Sources: Simply Safe Dividends, Gurufocus, CSImarketing)
3M's wide moat portfolio of products, backed by its legendary R&D efficiency, and led by new CEO Michael Roman (former COO and over 30-year company veteran), has allowed the company to deliver industry leading profitability and returns on invested capital. ROIC is a good proxy for quality management and a good corporate culture dedicated to investing shareholder capital wisely.
As a result of its great business model and adaptive corporate culture, 3M has delivered over 100 years of uninterrupted dividends and grown the payout for 60 consecutive years. Or to put another way, 3M is the bluest of blue-chips and a true sleep well at night or SWAN stock. One whose management is guiding for strong long-term growth to continue.
Long-Term Growth Guidance (Through 2023)
3%-5% organic local currency sales growth 8%-11% growth in earnings per share 20% return on invested capital (three times the industry average) 100% free cash flow conversion (EPS growth translates to dividend growth) And lest we forget 3M's recent selloff is actually going to help management achieve its long-term growth goals. That's because it just authorized a $10 billion buyback program , $2 to $4 billion of which is slated for 2019. If shares languish at these levels or fall further, I'd expect the figure to be closer to $4 billion or nearly 4% of its shares at current prices.
But 3M is hardly one to turn to financial engineering to drive its long-term growth. The company continues to execute on its proven track record of smart M&A including the recently announced $1 billion acquisition of M*Modal. This company is being acquired to strengthen 3M's healthcare information business and is a leader in cloud-computing AI driven conversational transcription services for doctors.
3M's healthcare information unit already serves over 8,000 health organizations worldwide and this deal, while not a needle mover in the short-term (M*Modal's TTM revenue is just $200 million) exemplifies 3M's strategy of steadily improving its core business units to achieve a stickier ecosystem with its customers (some of who have decades-long relationships with the company).
The M*Modal acquisition exemplifies 3M's recent focus on smaller and more focused acquisitions. Since 2012 it's made 12 purchases totalling $7.7 billion (average of $640 million each). This shows that management is not interested in splashy (and difficult to pull off) M&A (70% to 90% of those deals fail according to the Harvard business review) but a more targeted approach that's less risky and ultimately more profitable.
Meanwhile, the company remains dedicated to its strong focus on R&D, which has helped it to achieve its success over the decades.
" We will continue to work to optimize our portfolio prioritizing resources to our most attractive opportunities. We will strengthen our innovation model and continue to invest in research and development , which enables us to create unique solutions that advance, enhance and improve outcomes for our customers." - Mike Roman (emphasis added)
3M plans to invest about 6% of revenue into R&D over the long-term (about double the industry median). R&D isn't just about improving or launching new products, it also helps to cut costs over the long-term (by as much as $600 million in recent years), which itself has boosted EPS by 1.5% on an annualized rate.
3M has 8,100 researchers operating in 36 global R&D labs around the world to support its 46 different technology platforms. These R&D operations are churning out 3,000 patents a year, to add to the company's 115,000 patent portfolio . What's more those patents are actually delivering great returns on investment. A 2017 study by Boston Consulting Group found that each R&D dollar 3M spends delivers 61% greater gross profit the next year compared to the top 10 companies in the survey . It's also 57% above most innovative tech firms.
Basically, that means that in recent years 3M's R&D efficiency has been the second best in corporate America, second only to Apple ( AAPL ). Specifically in 2016 3M earned $8.88 in next year gross profit per $1 in R&D spend. Analysts currently expect that to average about $8.75 going forward, indicating that 3M's super efficient R&D results will continue.
Combine that laser like R&D focus with about 120,000 customer interactions per year and that helps 3M prioritize faster growing business lines. Over the next five years, that means boosting R&D by over 300% for 12 strategic businesses that are expected to generate 10% to 15% CAGR sales growth.
(Source: investor presentation)
In the future the company plans to focus its resources on fast growing secular trends including the internet of things (mostly safety products), electric cars, smart infrastructure, renewable energy/smart grids, and pollution control (huge growth markets in emerging markets like India and China).
As a result here's what management expects to achieve over the next five years.
(Source: investor presentation)
3M plans to take 3% to 5% organic sales growth (roughly in line with global GDP growth) and supplement that with 1% to 3% sales growth through M&A. The major acquisition targets are in its healthcare, safety & graphics, and industrial segments. Add to that 2% to 3% margin expansion (cost cutting including through R&D derived synergies) and you get 6% to 11% EPS (and FCF) growth.
Then add back the companies historical buyback rate ( 2.2% average over the last five years) and management should easily achieve its 8% to 11% EPS and FCF target and possibly even exceed it. That's because management's guidance is predicated on just 3% global GDP growth which is actually below what the both the IMF and OECD currently expect through 2020.
(Source: Forexlive) - note Nov 2018 estimate
In fact, the current 10-year analyst consensus is for precisely 9.5% long-term EPS and FCF/share growth. While analysts can always be wrong, in this case, they (and I) agree that management's long-term growth forecasts are reasonable.
Management's total five-year goal involves about $60 billion in operating cash flow and raising $5 billion to $15 billion in net debt. The capital allocation plan calls for spending 30% of operating cash flow on R&D and organic capex, 30% on dividends and 40% on M&A and opportunistic share buybacks.
(Source: investor presentation)
The bottom line is that, while 3M may be facing some headwinds in 2019, the industry leading management team is poised to do what it has always done. Adapt and overcome to whatever challenges the company faces, in order to deliver safe and growing dividends with clockwork like regularity.
That's a proven formula that has resulted in market crushing total returns over the past three decades.
MMM Total Return Price data by YCharts S&P 500 CAGR Total Return Since 1990: 9.4% 3M CAGR Total Returns Since 1990: 11.9% Over the last 28 years, 3M has beaten the market by 25% annually. But given the company's current long-term plans and a great growth runway to execute on, I actually expect that 3M's future returns will be far stronger. In fact, I expect that 3M will outperform the S&P 500 by about 50% over the coming 10 years.
2. Dividend Profile: Attractive Yield, Strong Dividend Growth, And Market-Beating Return Potential The heart of any good income investment is the dividend profile which consists of three parts, yield, payout safety, and long-term growth potential. Combined with valuation this is what determines total returns over time.
Company Yield TTM FCF Payout Ratio 10 Year Projected EPS/Dividend Growth 10 Year Potential Annual Total Return (Assuming No Valuation Changes) Valuation Adjusted Total Return Potential
3M 3.0% 69% 8% to 11% 11% to 14% 12.8% to 15.8% S&P 500 2.2% 33% 6.4% 8.6% 5% to 9.5% (Sources: management guidance, Simply Safe Dividends, Gurufocus, Fast Graphs, Morningstar, Vanguard, Yardeni Research, Gordon Dividend Growth Model, Dividend Yield Theory, Moneychimp, Kiplinger's, Factset Research)
For the first time in three years 3M is offering a 3% yield, which is nearly 50% above that of the S&P 500 (itself at multi-year highs). More importantly that dividend is rock solid (Simply Safe Dividend Safety Score 86/100 = "very safe").
That score is based on two key factors. First is the fact that 3M's FCF payout ratio, while above the 60% or below we like to see for industrial companies, is far from dangerously unsustainable, nor a determinant to management's long-term growth objectives.
The other half of the dividend safety equation is the balance sheet. In a capital intensive and M&A heavy sector such as this, you want to make sure that a company's debt levels are modest.
Company Net Debt/EBITDA Interest Coverage Ratio Current Ratio S&P Credit Rating Average Interest Rate
3M 1.6 16.4 2.0 AA- 1.7% Industry Average 2.2 28.8 1.9 NA NA (Sources: Simply Safe Dividends, Gurufocus, Fast Graphs, Morningstar)
3M's balance sheet is a fortress, with below average leverage, strong interest coverage, and a current ratio (short-term assets/short-term liabilities) of 2 (above 1 is safe).
Now it should be pointed out that 3M's net debt stands at $11.3 billion . Management's latest plans call for potentially raising that by as much as $15 billion over the next five years. That's the maximum debt the company is willing to add to the balance sheet, including more aggressive M&A activity going forward.
How worried should investors be? Not at all. Assuming that EBITDA grows at management's five-year mid-range guidance (8.5%) that would mean that in 2023 3M's net leverage ratio would be between 1.3 and 2.1. The worst case scenario is still slightly less leverage than its peers, and the midrange guidance calls for 3M retaining the same leverage ratio it has now. With one of the strongest balance sheets on Wall Street, 3M's access to low cost borrowing (cheaper than the US Treasury's 2.9% average) should remain intact. That's especially true given that 3M sells long-term bonds overseas where interest rates are still near zero and likely to remain far lower than in the US for the foreseeable future.
Over the long-term, the dividend will grow at the same rate as earnings and cash flow. For 3M that's 8% to 11%, which is well above the S&P 500's historical dividend growth rate of 6.4% . Combine better yield with faster dividend growth and you get superior total returns of 11% to 14%, assuming no valuation changes.
For context the market's historical total return is 9.2% , and from today's attractive valuations the S&P 500 is likely to deliver about 9.5% total returns over the next decade. That's based on the same valuation-adjusted total return model that Brookfield Asset Management ( BAM ) has been using for decades. Vanguard is less optimistic and assumes the S&P 500 will deliver 5% to 8% CAGR returns over the coming years. In either case, even assuming the current valuation remains constant, 3M will easily beat those results.
But in fact, 3M is currently undervalued, which means investors can likely expect long-term total returns of 13% to 16%, better than what it's delivered over the past three decades.
3. Valuation: A Great Time To Add This Dividend King To Your Portfolio MMM Total Return Price data by YCharts It's been a grim year for 3M investors, with the stock underperforming the S&P 500, which itself is having its worst year since 2008. However, while such returns can cause much wailing and gnashing of teeth for some, value investors get excited when they see charts like this. That's because 3M is now trading at its best valuation in three years.
Forward PE 5-Year Average Forward PE 20-Year Average PE Implied 10-Year EPS Growth Rate Expected EPS Growth Rate
17.5 19.9 20.9 4.5% 8% to 11% (Sources: Simply Safe Dividends, Fast Graphs, Benjamin Graham, management guidance)
The company's forward PE is below its five and 20 year average. The current PE ratio is implying about 5% long-term EPS growth, well below what either management or analysts (including myself) expect. This means that the stock is potentially poised for multiple expansion that could drive total returns faster than even the yield + long-term EPS/dividend growth predicted by the Gordon Dividend Growth Model (relatively accurate since 1956).
How much of a valuation boost might 3M investors see over time? To answer that I turn to my favorite valuation method for dividend stocks, dividend yield theory or DYT. Since 1966 asset manager/newsletter publisher Investment Quality Trends has exclusively been using this approach. As a result, they've managed to deliver decades of market-beating total returns with 10% less volatility to boot.
(Source: Investment Quality Trends)
DYT is a dead simple but highly effective strategy based on the principle of mean reversion. Here's how it works. Using long time periods, that incorporate various economic/industry and interest rate environments, you estimate a stock's historical yield. This tells you what valuation a stock typically returns to, and thus approximates fair value.
Yield 5-Year Average Yield 13-Year Median Yield Fair Value Yield Discount To Fair Value 3.0% 2.5% 2.5% 2.5% 17% (Sources: Simply Safe Dividends, Gurufocus, Dividend Yield Theory)
3M's five-year average yield and 13-year median yield (which includes the worst recession since WWII) are identical and show that even factoring in slower growth next year and even a future recession, a 2.5% yield is roughly the fair value yield for 3M. Under the Buffett principle of "it's better to buy a wonderful company at a fair price than a fair company at a wonderful price" I can endorse buying this blue-chip at a yield of 2.5% or better.
Today 3M's 3% yield means that it's about 17% undervalued according to this time-tested and highly lucrative valuation/investing approach.
Upside To Fair Value 10-Year CAGR Valuation Boost Total Return Potential (No Valuation Change) Valuation-Adjusted Total Return Potential
20% 1.8% 11% to 14% 12.8% to 15.8% (Sources: Dividend Yield Theory, Simply Safe Dividends, Gurufocus, management guidance)
For 3M to return to fair value means shares would rise 20% faster than EPS/dividend growth over time. For my long-term return model (total return = yield + long-term EPS/dividend growth + valuation boost) I use a 10-year time horizon.
This means that 3M's shares can be expected to rise about 2% faster than EPS and dividends over the coming decade. That ultimately equates to a total return potential of 3% yield + 8% to 11% EPS/FCF/dividend growth + 1.8% CAGR valuation boost or 12.8% to 15.8%. For the Deep Value Dividend Growth Portfolio I set a high standard of 13+% TRP. 3M finally hits that target with about 14.5% expected total returns over the next decade. This is why I'm thrilled to add it to the portfolio and recommend that all long-term income growth investors (who are comfortable with its risk profile) consider buying it as well.
Bottom Line: 3M Is Now A Fantastic Long-Term Investing Opportunity I'm not a market timer and I can't guarantee you that 3M has finished falling (no one rings a bell at the bottom). However, what I can assure you is that this legendary dividend king's fundamentals remain excellent, its management team and corporate culture top notch, its balance sheet a fortress, and its long-term dividend growth thesis as strong as ever.
Could 3M fall even further? Sure. The current valuation is the best in three years but during the darkest days of the Financial Crisis the yield hit a peak of 4.8%. But given the actual global macro fundamentals today, the chances of 3M plunging another 39% to offer that same once in a life time yield are slim.
Today 3M's 3% yield means it's about 17% undervalued, and likely to deliver about 14.5% long-term total returns. That's about 50% better than what the S&P 500 is likely to generate over the next decade. When I see a world class blue-chip (and a dividend king) trading at such a margin of safety, and offering such strong total return potential, it's not hard to give it a "strong buy" recommendation.
That's why I added a starter position in 3M to the Deep Valued Dividend Growth Portfolio and will happily keep adding more every month should the stock fall further or remain at its current price. I recommend that any income growth investors consider also adding this legendary dividend king to their portfolio because with quality of this caliber, at these prices, great long-term returns are all but guaranteed.
